ai.headline: Slack now shares some personal data with advertisers for targeting ads elsewhere
ai.summary: Slack says it may now share identifiers and internet activity information with third-party advertisers to target ads on non-Slack websites, apps, and services. California users gain a right to know about and opt out of this sharing, and the policy now states that some personal information is collected and disclosed for "business purposes" under California's CPRA amendment.
ai.what_you_can_do: California consumers can request to know about and opt out of the sharing of their personal information for delivering advertisements on non-Slack websites, using the request methods in the policy (privacy@slack.com or the linked form).

ai.headline: Slack updates its Irish office address in privacy policy
ai.summary: Slack Technologies Limited's listed address in Ireland changed from Level 1, Block A Nova Atria in Sandyford to Salesforce Tower in North Dock, Dublin. This is only a contact address update and does not change how user data is handled.

ai.headline: Slack adds ways for California users to opt out of data sharing
ai.summary: Slack now explains how California users can opt out of having their activity shared, either by turning on a Global Privacy Control in their browser or by contacting Slack using the email address or phone number linked to their account. This clarifies existing CCPA rights rather than adding new data uses.

removed: Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Cross-Border Privacy Rules System And Privacy Recognition For Processors. Slack’s privacy practices, described in this Privacy Policy, comply with the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (“APEC”) Cross Border Privacy Rules (“CBPR”) system and the Privacy Recognition for Processors (“PRP”). The APEC CBPR system provides a framework for organizations to ensure protection of personal data transferred among participating APEC economies and the PRP demonstrates an organization’s ability to provide effective implementation of a personal data controller’s privacy obligations related to the processing of personal information. More information about the APEC framework can be found here. If you have an unresolved privacy or data use concern related to our APEC CBPR or PRP certifications that we have not addressed satisfactorily, you may contact our third-party dispute resolution provider.
